_about: Role-based question plans written by Claude for the three official demo roles. Used as the demo assessments' questions and replayed by FixtureLLM when drafting questions for these roles without a candidate. Must-have requirements come first, so trimming to 5 questions still covers them.

questions.question: To start, tell me about your background and a project where you built a real feature with JavaScript or TypeScript.
questions.rationale: Warm-up that checks for real feature work beyond tutorials, the first must-have.

questions.question: In a React app you built, how did you handle state and data fetching, and was there a performance problem you had to fix?
questions.rationale: Tests depth in state management and data fetching rather than familiarity with React.

questions.question: Walk me through a REST API endpoint you designed in Node.js or similar. What was the trickiest part?
questions.rationale: The role maintains merchant-facing REST APIs; this checks real API design decisions.

questions.question: Tell me about a database schema you designed. Which tables and indexes did you choose, and why?
questions.rationale: Checks schema design and query thinking, ideally PostgreSQL, a must-have for the backend half of the role.

questions.question: How have branches, pull requests and code reviews worked on a team you've been part of?
questions.rationale: The squad ships through pull requests and reviews; checks collaborative Git habits.

questions.question: Tell me about a time something you built broke in production. What did you do in the moment, and what changed afterwards?
questions.rationale: Engineers debug production issues and own features end to end; shows ownership and operational habits.

questions.question: How would you explain a technical trade-off to a merchant who isn't an engineer?
questions.rationale: FalconPay engineers explain trade-offs to merchants and non-engineers.

questions.question: To start, tell me a little about your background and what draws you to marketing for Gen Z shoppers.
questions.rationale: Easy warm-up; also shows how clearly the candidate communicates.

questions.question: Tell me about a social media account or campaign you ran. What did you change, and what happened as a result?
questions.rationale: Looks for hands-on TikTok or Instagram work with results, the core of the role.

questions.question: How did you know whether a post was working? Which numbers did you look at, and what did you do with them?
questions.rationale: Checks whether the candidate reads reach and engagement and acts on them.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you juggled several deadlines at once. How did you keep track of everything?
questions.rationale: The graduate program rotates across many deliverables and deadlines.

questions.question: If you had to plan a TikTok campaign for Gen Z shoppers in the UAE on a small budget, what would you try first?
questions.rationale: Campaign thinking is a screening focus; a situational question works even without prior campaigns.

questions.question: How would you brief a content creator so they deliver what you need, on time, for a SouqBloom campaign?
questions.rationale: Working with creators and agencies is a core responsibility.

questions.question: Which tools do you use to make short videos or graphics, and what's something you made that you're proud of?
questions.rationale: Nice-to-have that speeds up content production in the role.

questions.question: To start, tell me about a finding from your own data work that changed what someone actually did.
questions.rationale: The team's analyses must lead to decisions by ops managers.

questions.question: Walk me through a SQL query you're proud of, for example one using joins or window functions.
questions.rationale: Joins, aggregations and window functions are named in the must-have.

questions.question: How would you design an A/B test to check whether a new rider bonus reduces evening delivery times?
questions.rationale: The intern helps design and read A/B tests on Dune Mobility's own metrics.

questions.question: Tell me about a dataset you cleaned in Python or R. What did you do about missing or messy values?
questions.rationale: Checks pandas-style cleaning and attention to detail with real data.

questions.question: Tell me about a time a number in your data looked wrong. How did you dig into why?
questions.rationale: Curiosity about why numbers look the way they do is a stated soft skill.

questions.question: Delivery times are often skewed by a few very late orders. How would you summarise them for an ops manager?
questions.rationale: Directly tests averages versus medians and distributions on the team's own kind of data.

questions.question: Finally, what makes you want to analyse ride-hailing and delivery data at Dune Mobility?
questions.rationale: Closes with motivation for the domain and the six-month internship.
